newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS - Russia govt to sell firms to repay wage debt.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Russia govt to sell firms to repay wage debt.

text.p: The Russian government, determined to repay trillions of roubles in overdue wages to public employees, said on Friday it had found new sources of funds and would not go to the markets for the money.
First Deputy Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin said President Boris Yeltsin had transferred his right to decide which companies could be sold off to the government.

"The Russian government received the right to decide itself, not through (presidential) decrees, the list of such companies, as the government has responsibility for repaying wages," Kudrin told a news conference. He said the Finance Ministry was working on a list of such companies.

The government is already in the middle of a major privatisation drive, with a tender for telecoms holding company Svyazinvest due to close and bids for a large stake in non-ferrous metals group Norilsk Nickel opening next week. Sales of stakes in several oil companies have already been announced.

Kudrin said the government, which has had to cut planned spending because of low tax revenues, would not increase borrowing money to raise extra funds and would would continue its policy of pushing down yields on Treasury bills.

President Yeltsin has made paying off wage arrears one of the government's prime tasks and ordered it to repay all overdue wages to the public sector by January 1, 1998, including paying the military by September 1.

Kudrin said the federal government owed 7.7 trillion roubles ($1.3 billion) in overdue wages. It has also promised to lend regional governments unable to cope with their own arrears, money to repay 50 percent of their debts.
Regional authorities owe 25.6 trillion roubles to public employees, the Finance Ministry said in a statement. It is not clear how much the federal government will help with.
Kudrin said the government would not allow arrears on pensions, paid off last month, to build up again.
And Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Sysuyev was quoted by Itar-Tass news agency as saying the government would raise pensions by 20 percent by December 1, 1997.
Kudrin said the regions were to present their plans on how to raise revenues by August 1 and the Finance Ministry would decide what regions it would help.
The wage arrears are part of a web of unpaid bills strangling the Russian economy. Millions of people have not been paid for months and demonstrations and protest marches are frequent.

On Thursday workers from Smolensk nuclear power station finished a 350 kilometre (220 miles) protest march to Moscow to receive a promise from First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov that an overdue 25 billion roubles would be allocated to their station at once.

Kudrin said tax collection had improved to 30 trillion roubles in June from 14 trillion in January, but was still less than the 33 or 34 trillion roubles the state needed to fulfil all its obligations.
He said the government would urge tax debtors to pay up.

The state had already squeezed 14.5 trillion roubles in taxes from RAO Gazprom natural gas monopoly and Kudrin said it planned to get five trillion roubles from national power utility RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES).
He also said the government planned to cut the number of its employees by 10 percent, or 3,000 people.
"We are sure that the liablities that the government has undertaken will be completely fullfilled," Kudrin said.
